- The cam status of the 31 single cams is displayed in "binary-coded" form in this parameter. l **Bit 15... 0 = 0000.0000.0000.0000:** 

   - Drive is not in a parameterized cam range or drive without safe reference (default) 

   - l **Bit 15... 0 = 0000.0000.0000.0001:** 

   - Drive is in cam range 1 

   - l **Bit 15... 0 = 0000.0000.0000.0010:** 

   - Drive is in cam range 2 

   - l **Bit 15... 0 = 0000.0000.0000.0011:** 

   - Drive is in cam range 3 

... 

- l **Bit 15... 0 = 0000.0000.0001.1110:** Drive is in cam range 30 

- l **Bit 15... 0 = 0000.0000.0001.1111:** Drive is in cam range 31

See also: Safely-Monitored Deceleration (SMD) **<u>P-0-3280.0.4 - Attributes</u>** <u>Ê</u> © Bosch Rexroth AG 2022 RS-7cfcba501de5d89d0a347e867524d482-1-en-US-4 DOK-INDRV*-GEN1-PARA**-RE15-EN-P **MPx-16 to MPx-21 and PSB, Parameters** P-0-3280.0.5, SMO: Max. tolerance time for different selection **<u>Allocation</u>** <u>Ê</u> **Function** This parameter defines the maximum allowed time within which the input signals may be different from the selection signals. # **MPx-16 to MPx-21 and PSB, Parameters** P-0-3280.0.7, SMO: SMD reaction time **<u>Allocation</u>** <u>Ê</u> **Function** 



This parameter serves to configure the "safety-monitored deceleration (SMD)" safety function based on the actual velocity. 

The "SMD-E reaction time" is the reaction time for the system (control and drive) in order that the command value input can be adjusted for the transfer to the selected special mode. After this time has elapsed, the parameterized deceleration ramp is monitored.

### **MPx-16 to MPx-21 and PSB, Parameters** 

P-0-3280.0.9, SMO: SMD deceleration 

RS-7cfcba501de5d89d0a347e867524d482-1-en-US-4 DOK-INDRV*-GEN1-PARA**-RE15-EN-P 





# **<u>Allocation</u>** <u>Ê</u> **Function** 

This parameter serves to configure the "safety-monitored deceleration (SMD)" safety function with trend monitoring based on the actual velocity. The parameter defines a deceleration threshold (bipolar) for switching between the safety technology operating statuses. 

- See also: Safely-Monitored Deceleration (SMD) **<u>P-0-3280.0.9 - Attributes</u>** <u>Ê</u> 

© Bosch Rexroth AG 2022 

### **MPx-16 to MPx-21 and PSB, Parameters** 

P-0-3280.0.10, SMO: SMD jerk 

RS-7cfcba501de5d89d0a347e867524d482-1-en-US-4 DOK-INDRV*-GEN1-PARA**-RE15-EN-P 





# **<u>Allocation</u>** <u>Ê</u> **Function** 

The parameter defines the maximum allowed jerk that is taken into account in the velocity envelope curve for monitoring the safety technology operating status change with the transition function "Safely-monitored deceleration based on actual velocity (SMDActVel)". 





With the value 0, the jerk is not taken into account. 

In the case of drive-controlled transition and use of the jerk (P-0-3280.0.10 > 0), the value in 

- l "P-0-3280.0.10" should be parameterized with the jerk limit value of the standard firmware in parameter "S-0-349, Bipolar jerk limit". 

- l "P-0-3280.0.9, SMO: Delay SMD" depending on the setting in "P-0-0119, Best possible shutdown" on the delay ramp of the standard firmware can be parameterized in "S-0-0372, Delay fast stop" or "S-0-429, Emergency stop delay". 

**<u>P-0-3280.0.10 - Attributes</u>** <u>Ê</u> 

© Bosch Rexroth AG 2022 

### **MPx-16 to MPx-21 and PSB, Parameters** 

P-0-3280.0.11, SMO: SMD reaction time, trend time, NO to standstill

# **<u>Allocation</u>** <u>Ê</u> **Function** 

In the feature "time-based trend monitoring", the parameter defines the reaction time of the system (drive and control) in the safety function "Safely monitored delay (SMD)" to adjust the command value specification for normal mode transition to special mode "Safe standstill". After the time defined in this parameter has elapsed, the parameterized delay ramp is monitored.

### **MPx-16 to MPx-21 and PSB, Parameters** 

P-0-3290.x.4, SMO: Safe position limit value, positive 

RS-7cfcba501de5d89d0a347e867524d482-1-en-US-4 DOK-INDRV*-GEN1-PARA**-RE15-EN-P 





# **<u>Allocation</u>** <u>Ê</u> **Function** 

The allowed travel range of an axis can be defined by position limit values. The "safe position limit value, positive" defines the maximum admissible position feedback value for "special operation safe motion n" (n = 1-16) in positive direction. 

Depending on the configuration in P-0-3290.x.1, the parameterized position limits (P-0-3290.x.4 and P-0-3290.x.5) are subject to dual-channel monitoring using the functions "Safely-monitored position (SMP)" (P-0-3290.x.1; bit 5 = 1) or "Safely-limited position (SLP)" (P-0-3290.x.1; bit 7 = 1 ). The following aspects have to be observed for use: 

- l Monitoring of the "Safely-monitored position (SLP)" and "Safely-limited position (SLP)" will not become effective before the drive has been safely homed (P-0-3256; bit 0). 

l If the safety function recognizes faulty behavior during "Safely-monitored position (SMP)" or "Safely-limited position (SLP)" monitoring, error message F7011 or F7012 are returned. The drive is shut down with the configured F7 error reaction (torque disable is not admissible as F7 error reaction for safety function "Safely-limited position (SLP)"). 

**<u>P-0-3290.x.4 - Attributes</u>** <u>Ê</u>

Depending on the configuration in "P-0-3290.x.1", the parameterized position limits (P-0-3290.x.4 and P-0-3290.x.5) are subject to dual-channel monitoring using the functions "Safely-monitored position (SMP)" (bit 5 = 1 in P-0-3290.x.1) or "Safely-limited position (SLP)" (bit 7 = 1 in P-0-3290.x.1). The following aspects have to be observed for use:

- l If the safety function recognizes faulty behavior during "Safely-monitored position (SMP)" or "Safely-limited position (SLP)" monitoring, error message F7011 or F7012 are returned. With this parameter, the nominal load of the holding system (P-0-3292.0.3) for static brake test can be loaded with a safety factor. Test torque = Nominal load × Safety factor = P-0-3292.0.3 × P-0-3292.0.4

> **<u>Allocation</u>** <u>Ê</u> **Function** The functional inputs 13... 16 (P-0-3329, Bit 12… 15) are accepted as dynamized functional signals. With activated dynamization (P-0-3332.0.4 > "0"), the signals (signal level = "1") must be provided with regular test pulses. ### **MPx-16 to MPx-21 and PSB, Parameters** 

P-0-3332.0.4, SMO: Functional inputs, periodic time of test pulses 





> **<u>Allocation</u>** <u>Ê</u> **Function** The functional inputs 13... 16 (P-0-3329; bit 12… 15) are accepted as dynamized functional signals. 

With activated dynamization (P-0-3332.0.4 > "0"), the signals (signal level = "1") must be provided with regular test pulses. 

In "P-0-3332.0.4", the period duration (ms) in which at least one test pulse has to be recognized can be set. If no test pulse has been recognized after expiration of the period duration, the dynamic input signals are zeroed and error F3361 is generated. 



With P-0-3332.0.4 = "0", dynamization is switched off and the concerned signals can be used as static input signals.

# **<u>Allocation</u>** <u>Ê</u> **Function** 

The "Special mode safe motion x (SMM x)" source signals from "P-0-3231, SMO: Operating status" are bit-encoded. Depending on the type of preferential configuration of the status word Safety bus, the status for special mode safe motion is contained there either with bit or binary coding. 

The coding function is parameterized in this parameter. If a value unequal to 0 is entered here, the coding in the "signal control for status word Safety bus"

### **MPx-16 to MPx-21 and PSB, Parameters** 

P-0-3340, SMO: Safety bus control word 

RS-7cfcba501de5d89d0a347e867524d482-1-en-US-4 DOK-INDRV*-GEN1-PARA**-RE15-EN-P 





> **<u>Allocation</u>** <u>Ê</u> **Function** This parameter is used to transmit control information of a safety control via safe bus communication as a part of the consumer connection. The evaluation of the individual bits of the "control word Safety bus" depends on the configuration of the IO mapper inputs (P-0-3330.x.y). 



Only preferential configurations are supported at present; therefore the "IO mapper inputs" are configured automatically. If "P-0-3340.0.1, SMO: Mask of Control word Safety-Bus" is used to mask bits, the respective bit of the control word is not implemented to the target parameter 1:1. A user-side setting for evaluation of the bit can be configured in the IO mapper.

### **MPx-16 to MPx-21 and PSB, Parameters** 

P-0-3340.0.1, SMO: Mask of control word, safety bus 





> **<u>Allocation</u>** <u>Ê</u> **Function** This parameter can be used to deactivate the preferential configuration of individual bits of "P-0-3340.0.0, SMO: Control word Safety-Bus". Bits thus deactivated can be used via the I/O configurator as desired. 



A value of "0" at the appropriate bit of this parameter deactivates the effect of the bit in "P-0-3345, SMO: Configuration Safety-Bus".

### **MPx-16 to MPx-21 and PSB, Parameters** 

P-0-3602.0.1, CiA301: COB-ID SYNC message 





|**Allocation**<br>Ê<br>**Function**|
|---|



This parameters implements the object 1005h "COB ID SYNC message" for the profile "CiA301". 

The object defines the COB ID of the synchronization object (SYNC). It also defines whether the device generates the Sync telegram. **Structure** 

## **Index 1005h, subindex 0 for "COB ID SYNC message"** 

|**Bit**|**Name/function**|**Comment**|
|---|---|---|
|28…0|**CAN ID**<br>80h|Die CAN ID of the Sync telegram is 80hby default.|
|29|**Frame**<br>0b: 11-bit CAN ID||
|30|**CANopen device generates the Sync telegram**<br>0b: CANopen device does not generate the Sync telegram<br>1b: CANopen device generates the Sync telegram|Generally, the CANopen master sends the Sync telegram. In this case, the<br>CANopen device is the receiver of the Sync telegram (**"Sync Consumer"**<br>and is then synchronized as slave via the Sync telegram by the master).<br>In special cases, the CANopen device can sent the Sync telegram and<br>allows other CANopen devices to synchronize with it (**"Sync Producer"**).|
|31|Not relevant||
|_Example:_|||



As **"Sync consumer"** , the object value is 00000080h by default. 

As **"Sync producer"** , the object value is 40000080h by default.

|P-0-3605.0.1, CiA301: Guard time|
|**Allocation**<br>Ê|
|**Function**|
|This parameters implements the object 100Ch"Guard time" for the profile "CiA301".|







The object contains the "Guard time" in milliseconds. 

Use the "Guard time" and the "Life time factor" to calculate the "life time" for the node guarding protocol to monitor the node as follows: 

Life time [ms] = Guard time [ms] × Life time factor 

Guard time: 100Ch (P-0-3605.0.1) Life time factor: 100Dh (P-0-3605.0.2) If the device is not queried by the master using the guarding telegram within the "life time", a monitoring error is generated. If the "life time" is "0", "node guarding" is disabled. When enabling the "node guarding", the "heartbeat consumer" and the "heartbeat producer" are disabled implicitly.

## **Function** 

This parameters implements the object 1016h "Consumer heartbeat time", subindex 1 "Consumer heartbeat time" for the profile "CiA301" 

As "heartbeat consumer", the slave monitors the "heartbeat" of the master. The object indexes the maximum cycle time expected by the "master heartbeat" in milliseconds. If the slave did not receive any "heartbeat" from the master within this period, a monitoring error is generated. **Structure** 

## **Index 1016h, subindex 1** 

|**Bit**|**Name/function**|**Comment**|
|---|---|---|
|15…0|**"Heartbeat time" in milliseconds [ms]**|If "Heartbeat consumer" is enabled, the "Node guarding" is disabled<br>implicitly.<br>Disable the "heartbeat consumer" with "heartbeat time"="0".|
|23…16|**"Master Node ID"**|If "Heartbeat consumer" is enabled, the "Node guarding" is disabled<br>implicitly.<br>Disable the "heartbeat consumer" with "master node ID"="0" or "master<br>node ID">"127".|
|31…24|Reserved (00h)||

## **Function** 

The parameters implement the objects from 1800h to 1803h "TPDO communication parameter", subindex 2 "Transmission type TPDO" for the profile "CiA301". 

The transmission method of the respective TPDO can be set via the parameter. 

|P<br>-<br>0<br>-<br>3614<br>.**0**.3<br>Index 1800h|, subindex 2 for TPDO**1**|
|---|---|
|P<br>-<br>0<br>-<br>3614<br>.**1**.3<br>Index 1801h|, subindex 2 for TPDO**2**|
|P<br>-<br>0<br>-<br>3614<br>.**2**.3<br>Index 1802h|, subindex 2 for TPDO**3**|
|P<br>-<br>0<br>-<br>3614<br>.**3**.3<br>Index 1803h|, subindex 2 for TPDO**4**|



**Supported transmission methods Type 0 synchronous, acyclic** The TPDO is sent by the slave if required ("event-driven") after the next Sync point. **Type 1 synchronous, cyclic** The TPDO is cyclically sent by the slave after each Sync point. **Type 252 synchronous, RTR-only** Data of the TDPO is refreshed in each Sync cycle. The TPDO is not actively send, only upon an RTR request. **Type 254 Synchronous, acyclic** The TPDO is sent by the slave only if required ("event-driven"). 



**"Event-driven"** : An event is available if data changed in the PDO. If data changes continuously, the "inhibit time" (subindex 3) (P-0- <u>3614.x.4) applies to ensure that the PDO is not sent more often than this inhibit time. If data changes rarely or not at all, the PDO is still sent</u> after the time "event timer" (subindex 5) (P-0-3614.x.5) elapses.

## **Function** 

The parameters implement the objects from 1800h to 1803h "TPDO communication parameter", subindex 3 "Inhibit time TPDO" for the profile "CiA301". Via the parameter, a minimum time span in microseconds [µs] can be defined for the "event-driven" TPDO. Even if the event occurs more often, the TPDO is not sent more often than this time span in order not to overload the field bus. 

- "Inhibit time TPDO" should be a multiple of 100 µs and lower than "event timer TPDO" (P-0-3614.x.6).

P-0-3614.x.200, TPDO on-event bit mask 

RS-7cfcba501de5d89d0a347e867524d482-1-en-US-4 DOK-INDRV*-GEN1-PARA**-RE15-EN-P 





# **<u>Allocation</u>** <u>Ê</u> 

## **Function** 

The parameter allows for an additional configuration for **"event-driven" TPDOs** for the "CiA301" profile for the objects 1800h to 1803h "TPDO communication parameter". 

The P-0-3614.x.200 provides a bit mask to define which bits of the TPDO are considered for generating an event for sending. By default all bits of the mask are set and all bits of the TPDO are considered for the generation of events. If a bit of the mask is set to **0** , a change of the bit at the same position in the TPDO does not generate an event anymore. 



**"Event-driven”:** An event is present when the data in the PDO has changed. This parameter allows to limit the generation of events to the change of certain data in the PDO. This can be used, for example, if only the change of a certain process date is relevant for the application. 

|P<br>-<br>0<br>-<br>3614<br>**.0**.200|Bit mask for "Event-driven" TPDO**1**|
|---|---|
|P<br>-<br>0<br>-<br>2614<br>**.1**.200|Bit mask for "Event-driven" PDO**2**|
|P<br>-<br>0<br>-<br>3614<br>**.2**.200|Bit mask for "Event-driven" TPDO**3**|
|P<br>-<br>0<br>-<br>3614<br>**.3**.200|Bit mask for "Event-driven" TPDO**4**|

|P<br>-<br>0<br>-<br>3615<br>.**0**.1|Index 1A00h, subindex 0 for TPDO**1**|
|---|---|
|P<br>-<br>0<br>-<br>3615<br>.**1**.1|Index 1A01h, subindex 0 for TPDO**2**|
|P<br>-<br>0<br>-<br>3615<br>.**2**.1|Index 1A02h, subindex 0 for TPDO**3**|
|P<br>-<br>0<br>-<br>3615<br>.**3**.1|Index 1A03h, subindex 0 for TPDO**4**|



## **Use** 

_Example:_ 

Number 0: Mapping disabled. The PDO is thus disabled. Number 1: Object of the subindex 1 is valid. 

Number 2: Objects of the subindices 1 to 2 are valid. 

8/18/2026 

Page 441 of 494 

Number 3: Objects of the subindices 1 to 3 are valid. 

Number 4: Objects of the subindices 1 to 4 are valid. 



Subindex 1 up to subindex 4 are the valid maximum. 

Proceed as follows for the PDO mapping: 

1. Set subindex 0 to "0" to delete all existing mapping objects in this PDO. 

2. Write from subindex 1 up to subindex N (N ≤ 4) with mapping objects. 

3. Set the subindex 0 to the number N.

P-0-3620.0.1, ECAT: Transmit PDO Mapping 

RS-7cfcba501de5d89d0a347e867524d482-1-en-US-4 DOK-INDRV*-GEN1-PARA**-RE15-EN-P 





# **<u>Allocation</u>** <u>Ê</u> 

## **Function** 

CAN over EtherCAT (CoE) object to /CiA301/ 

Index 1A00h "Transmit PDO Mapping Parameter" 

Subindex 0 - "number of mapped application objects in PDO" 

When this parameter is read, the number of valid entries of application objects in the subindices is returned. When a certain value N (0 ≤ N ≤ 16) is written to the parameter, the entries of application objects available in subindices 1 to N are mapped to the PDO channel. Subindices N+1 to 16 become invalid. See also parameter description "P-0-3621.0.1" 

|**Value**|**Description**|
|---|---|
|0|Mapping deactivated|
|1|Subindex 1 valid|
|2|Subindices 1 to 2 valid|
|3|Subindices 1 to 3 valid|
|......|......|
|16|Subindices 1 to 16 valid|



- **<u>P-0-3620.0.1 - Attributes</u>** <u>Ê</u>

# **<u>Allocation</u>** <u>Ê</u> **Function** 

SoC threshold value counter. It is increased by the value “8” whenever the controlled node (CN) detects a "loss of SoC". It is reduced by the value “1”, if no "loss of SoC" was detected within a cycle. 

**<u>P-0-3634.0.3 - Attributes</u>** <u>Ê</u>

### **MPx-16 to MPx-21 and PSB, Parameters** 

P-0-3634.0.4, EPL: Loss SoC: Threshold 





# **<u>Allocation</u>** <u>Ê</u> 

## **Function** 

If the “Loss SoC: Threshold Cnt” exceeds the threshold value set here, the drive changes to the "Pre-Operational 1" state and the threshold value counter (0x1C0Bsub2) is reset to 0. 

The threshold value counter is deactivated when the threshold value is set to 0 here. In this case, the drive does not execute an error reaction upon "Loss of SoC". **<u>P-0-3634.0.4 - Attributes</u>** <u>Ê</u> 

© Bosch Rexroth AG 2022

P-0-3635.0.3, EPL: CRC Error: Threshold Cnt 





# **<u>Allocation</u>** <u>Ê</u> **Function** 

The parameter writes to the CRC threshold value counter. The CRC threshold value counter is increased by the value “8” whenever the controlled node (CN) detects a "CRC error". It is reduced by the value “1”, if no "CRC error" was detected within a cycle. **<u>P-0-3635.0.3 - Attributes</u>** <u>Ê</u>

### **MPx-16 to MPx-21 and PSB, Parameters** 

P-0-3635.0.4, EPL: CRC Error: Threshold 





# **<u>Allocation</u>** <u>Ê</u> 

## **Function** 

If the CN exceeds the set threshold value of the parameter "CRC Error: Threshold Cnt", the drive executes an error reaction and the threshold value counter (0x1C0Fsub2) is reset to the value “0”. 

The threshold value counter is deactivated when the threshold value is set to the value “0”. In this case, the drive does not execute an error reaction upon

### **MPx-16 to MPx-21 and PSB, Parameters** 

P-0-3647.0.7, ECAT: Calc and Copy Time (Outputs) 





> **<u>Allocation</u>** <u>Ê</u> **Function** The command value (process data master → slave) is cyclically received by the slave from the EtherCAT FPGA and processed. This takes place one position controller cycle before the Sync1 event. For this reason, the EtherCAT telegram with the command value is to be received one position controller cycle before the Sync1 event. The time of a position controller cycle varies depending on the device derivative and performance. This is designated "Calc and copy time (outputs)". 

CAN over EtherCAT (CoE) object 

Index 1C32h - "Output Sync manager parameter" 

Subindex 6 - "Calc and copy time (outputs)" The "Calc and copy time (outputs)" - object 1C32h subindex 6 - before the Sync1 event and the "Calc and copy time (inputs)" - object 1C33h subindex 6 - after the Sync1 event together form a protection time. During this protection time, the master must not send the EtherCAT telegram. 

See also parameter description "P-0-3648.0.7" 

**<u>P-0-3647.0.7 - Attributes</u>** <u>Ê</u>

### **MPx-16 to MPx-21 and PSB, Parameters** 

P-0-3930, C7600 Command Create parameter image 

RS-7cfcba501de5d89d0a347e867524d482-1-en-US-4 DOK-INDRV*-GEN1-PARA**-RE15-EN-P 





> **<u>Allocation</u>** <u>Ê</u> **Function** Parameter "P-0-3930" can be used to generate an image of the current drive parameter values in a file on the external memory card (SnapShot). The name of this file is always "SnapShot.par". The file is stored to the "Temp" folder of the memory card. This parameter image can comprise the data of a single axis (single backup) or the data of all axes connected in the CCD group (complete backup). The content of the parameter image can be created based on the parameter list "S-0-0017" or "S-0-0192". Image generation is configured in parameter "P-0- <u>3931".</u> 

The following information is saved from all ident numbers listed in the selected reference parameter: 

l Ident number 

l Unit 

l Attribute l Operating data The backup file is stored in "sercos ASCII" format, i.e., it can be opened and evaluated in "IndraWorks". Execution of the command can be aborted by deleting the command. If execution of the command is aborted, the associated backup file is deleted. The command "Create parameter image" is only available for drive derivatives with a file system on the SD card. **<u>P-0-3930 - Attributes</u>** <u>Ê</u> 

© Bosch Rexroth AG 2022 

### **MPx-16 to MPx-21 and PSB, Parameters** 

P-0-3931, Control word of Create parameter image 

RS-7cfcba501de5d89d0a347e867524d482-1-en-US-4 DOK-INDRV*-GEN1-PARA**-RE15-EN-P 





# **<u>Allocation</u>** <u>Ê</u> **Function** 

The parameter "P-0-3931" is the control word for parameter image creation. 

The following settings can be made: 

|**Byte**|**Designation/function**|**Comment**|
|---|---|---|
|0|**0xFF:**Backup of all axes<br>Logical axis number: Backup of a single axis|Default: Backup of all axes<br>Examples:<br>**0x00:**Backup of master axis<br>**0x02:**Backup of second slave axis|
|1|**0x01:**Create parameter image "SnapShot"<br>Basis:S<br>-<br>0<br>-<br>0017<br>**0x02:**Create parameter image "SnapShot"<br>Basis:S<br>-<br>0<br>-<br>0192|Default: 0x01<br>Permitted settings: 0x01, 0x02|



_Byte assignment of parameter P - 0 - 3931_ 



During running execution of command "Generate parameter image", the configuration cannot be changed (input is ignored). If an invalid configuration is entered, the default setting takes effect.

RS-7cfcba501de5d89d0a347e867524d482-1-en-US-4 DOK-INDRV*-GEN1-PARA**-RE15-EN-P 





**MPx-16 to MPx-21 and PSB, Parameters**

# **<u>Allocation</u>** <u>Ê</u> 

## **Function** 

Parameter "P-0-3933" contains the character string of the service password. 

After "Load basic parameter", the password: "serviceWeb" is active. The service password is used by the drive's ServiceTools (IMST, IDST). 



It can be set to prevent unauthorized persons from logging in as "service" user and gaining access to all service dialogs. 

A service password is set by writing the parameter "P-0-3933" via the commissioning software "IndraWorks Ds". This is also where the encryption of the password takes place. This is checked during access to the IDST.

**MPx-16 to MPx-21 and PSB, Parameters** P-0-4004, Magnetizing current **<u>Allocation</u>** <u>Ê</u> **Function** In case of asynchronous motors, this parameter is used to enter the nominal magnetizing current defined by Bosch Rexroth. The actually flowing magnetizing current in the basic speed range results from multiplying the value of "P-0-4004" by "P-0-0532, Premagnetization factor". In the fieldweakening range, the magnetizing current is reduced with increasing speed, starting from the value of this product by the field controller. 



Writing the correct value to this parameter: 





- l In case of Rexroth motors of the 2AD, ADF series as well as in case of linear and rotary kit motors, by loading the motor parameters via the commissioning software "IndraWorks Ds/D/MLD". 

> l In case of other asynchronous motors, by manual input according to the manufacturer's specification. 

- l In case of synchronous motors, the parameter is not used and automatically set to Aeff = 0. 

See also Functional Description "Motor, Mechanical Axis System, Measuring Systems" **<u>P-0-4004 - Attributes</u>** <u>Ê</u>

### P-0-4010, Load inertia 

RS-7cfcba501de5d89d0a347e867524d482-1-en-US-4 DOK-INDRV*-GEN1-PARA**-RE15-EN-P 





# **<u>Allocation</u>** <u>Ê</u> **Function** 

This parameter is provided for the (motor-related) load inertia reduced to the motor. It is used for: 

- l Automatic control loop setting (C1800) 

- l encoderless, flow-controlled motor operation (FXC) 

If none of the above cases is used, it is not necessary to enter a value. Depending on bit 9 of parameter "P-0-4, Motor type", the value has a different meaning: 

- l Load inertia, motor-related (without rotor inertia) for rotary motors 

- l Load mass (without primary part mass) for linear motors 

See also Functional Description "Automatic setting of axis control"

### **MPx-16 to MPx-21 and PSB, Parameters** 

P-0-4013, Current limit value of demagnetization 

RS-7cfcba501de5d89d0a347e867524d482-1-en-US-4 DOK-INDRV*-GEN1-PARA**-RE15-EN-P 





> **<u>Allocation</u>** <u>Ê</u> **Function** This parameter contains a percent value which is referring to parameter "S-0-0109, Motor peak current" for synchronous motors. If this percentage value is multiplied with the value of "S-0-0109", the result is the current limit value. If the electric current limit value is exceeded, the magnets of the synchronous motor risk being permanently demagnetized. 

In case the limit value is exceeded, the power output stage of the controller is temporarily disabled to protect the motor, until the electric current has fallen below the limit value again. Warning E8028 is generated in the disabled state. 



The correct value is written to this parameter as follows: 

- l In case of Rexroth motors with encoder data memory: 

Automatic when controller is switched on. 

- l In case of Rexroth motors without encoder data memory: 

By loading the motor parameters with commissioning software "IndraWorks Ds/D/MLD". 

- l In case of other motors: 

By manual input according to the manufacturer's specification. 

See also functional description "Limitations"

### **MPx-16 to MPx-21 and PSB, Parameters** 

P-0-4030, Axis configuration for multi-axis device 

RS-7cfcba501de5d89d0a347e867524d482-1-en-US-4 DOK-INDRV*-GEN1-PARA**-RE15-EN-P 





# **<u>Allocation</u>** <u>Ê</u> 

## **Function** 

This parameter can be used to deactivate the hardware of an axis of a multi-axis device, i.e. the hardware of an axis (output stage, etc.) is not available for the firmware. This reduces the number of present axes of a multi-axis device. 

As a result, the assignment of the firmware axis to the hardware axis may change. If the hardware of the second axis is deactivated, there will be the following axis assignment of firmware to existing hardware: 

|**Firmware axis**|**Hardware axis**|
|---|---|
|1|1|
|2|3|
|3|4|
|(4)||



_Assignment of Firmware Axis to Hardware Axis_ 

## **Function** 



If an axis is to be deactivated or reactivated via this parameter, the device must be switched off and on again or "S01350, C6400 reboot command" must be executed after a value has been written to the parameter. Thereafter, the parameters of the existing axes are invalid. As a result, the existing axes must be re-parameterized. 

The default setting is activation of all existing axes of a device. At least one axis of a device must remain active. 

## **Function** 



With the double-axis control section, only the second axis can be deactivated!

l In case of Rexroth motors with encoder data memory, when the control voltage of the drive is switched on.

### **MPx-16 to MPx-21 and PSB, Parameters** 

P-0-4035, Thermal time constant of motor 

RS-7cfcba501de5d89d0a347e867524d482-1-en-US-4 DOK-INDRV*-GEN1-PARA**-RE15-EN-P 





# **<u>Allocation</u>** <u>Ê</u> 

## **Function** 

The thermal time constant of the motor is the time after which the motor housing has reached 63% of its final temperature if its cooling type is set to the standard value (see table) and the current in the motor winding is constant. 

In the firmware-internal motor temperature model, the value forms the basis for determining the cooling-type-dependent effective motor housing time constant: 

l In case of motors with invariable cooling type, the value corresponds to the effective motor housing time constant. 

l In case of motors with variable cooling type, the effective motor housing time constant is determined via "P-0-4035" and "P-0-0640, Cooling type". 

|**Motor type**|**Standard cooling type**|**Notes**|
|---|---|---|
|MSK, MHD, MKD, MKE|Non-ventilated|Cooling type variable: "P<br>-<br>0<br>-<br>0640<br>,Cooling type" must be set according to<br>the implemented cooling type|
|MAD, MAL, 2AD|Ventilated|Cooling type not variable: "P<br>-<br>0<br>-<br>0640<br>,Cooling type" is inactive|
|MAF, ADF, MBS, MBT, 1MB, MLF, LSF|Liquid-cooled|Cooling type not variable: "P<br>-<br>0<br>-<br>0640<br>,Cooling type" is inactive|
|Third-party motor|Unknown|Is considered to have no variable cooling type: "P<br>-<br>0<br>-<br>0640<br>,Cooling type"<br>is inactive!|



_Standard Cooling Types of Motors_ 



The motor temperature model uses a time constant for the heating of the motor winding (P-0-4034) and a time constant for the heating of the motor housing (P-0-4035). 

See also Functional Description "Current and Torque/Force Limitation"

### **MPx-16 to MPx-21 and PSB, Parameters** 

P-0-4036, Rated motor speed 





# **<u>Allocation</u>** <u>Ê</u> 

## **Function** 

## **Three-phase asynchronous motor:** 

The rated speed of an asynchronous motor is achieved by operation at three-phase supply with a rated voltage and rated frequency providing the rated torque at the motor shaft. 

## **Three-phase synchronous motor:** 

The rated speed of a synchronous motor is achieved by operation at three-phase supply with a rated voltage and rated frequency. 

See also Functional Description "Motor control" 



IndraDrive drive system supply three-phase AC motors with three-phase and variable voltage and variable frequency. The level of DC bus voltage limits the maximum supply voltage for the motor and defines the transition from the basic speed range to the field weakening range if the motor velocity (speed) is to be further increased. 

8/18/2026 

Page 481 of 494 

The level of DC bus voltage depends on: 

> l Voltage of the three-phase network to be in case of unregulated supply 

> l Supply unit for regulated supply 

At Rexroth motors, the DC bus voltage of DC540V is the reference value for the rated speed. This voltage is generated at unregulated supply of the drive system with a supply voltage of 3xAC400V(-5%). 



The correct value is written to this parameter as follows: 

- l In case of Rexroth motors with encoder data memory: Automatic when controller is switched on. 

- l In case of Rexroth motors without encoder data memory: 

By loading the motor parameters with commissioning software "IndraWorks Ds/D/MLD". 

- l In case of other motors: 

By manual input according to the manufacturer's specification.

P-0-4043, Rotor time constant 

RS-7cfcba501de5d89d0a347e867524d482-1-en-US-4 DOK-INDRV*-GEN1-PARA**-RE15-EN-P 





> **<u>Allocation</u>** <u>Ê</u> **Function** This parameter is only active with asynchronous motors. It has considerable influence on the torque generation of the motor. It defines significantly the "slip" under load. 



"Slip" is the difference of the rotational frequency of the electric rotary field in the stator divided by the number of pole pairs of the motor, and the mechanical rotational frequency of the rotor. 

The value for"P-0-4043" is motor-specific and for asynchronous Rexroth motors is made available via the commissioning software (e.g., IndraWorks) or via the Intranet output of the manufacturer-side data base DriveBase!

## **Function** 

Parameter "P-0-4057" is an image of the sequential block inputs. 

Triggered by an external switching signal, the switching signal-dependent block advance allows the transition to a sequential block. Two sequential block inputs are available as input for this switching signal: 

P-0-4057; Bit 0 -> sequential block cam 1 

The drive switches to the next travel block n+1 as soon as the input for sequential block cam 1 changes from "0" to "1". P-0-4057; Bit 1 -> sequential block cam 2 

The drive switches to the block following the next travel block n+2 as soon as the input for sequential block cam 2 changes from "0" to "1". See also functional description "Positioning block mode" **<u>P-0-4057 - Attributes</u>** <u>Ê</u>

### **MPx-16 to MPx-21 and PSB, Parameters** 



P-0-4084, Application: Profile type **<u>Allocation</u>** <u>Ê</u> **Function** With the setting in "P-0-4084", the active application profile in the drive is selected. By means of the active profile, different profile-specific functions in the drive are activated and the related parameters detected. If the active application profile is changed after switching on, the drive may need to be restarted. This is indicated by command error C0299 on switchover to operating mode "OM". The selected application profile defines the active control and status word of the drive. Additional functions may be added (CiA402 profile) or the behavior of functions may change. 

By means of the selected profile, default settings for various parameters can be defined: 

l Preselection of the operation modes or default values set in the drive

## **<u>P-0-4088, Master communication: Drive configuration : bit 5 = 0:</u>** 

The drive configuration switches in the parameter mode and reconfigures the I/O according to the described confugration. The configuration is not stored. By deactivating the command, the originally I/O configuration and the originally master communication are active again. 

## **<u>P-0-4088, Master communication: Drive configuration : bit 5 = 1:</u>** 

The drive does not reconfigures the I/O assignment. 

Is the drive in parameter mode, it switches automatically into the operation mode. The master communication is active again., by deactivating the command. **<u>P-0-4085 - Attributes</u>** <u>Ê</u>

This parameter contains the gateway address which is required within the scope of IP communication for the Ethernet-based master communication (EtherNet/IP and PROFINET). 

When an IP package (Internet Protocol) is transmitted, the network part of the target IP address and the network mask are compared. If they do not match, the IP package is transmitted to the gateway IP address. 



Parameter changes do not become effective before the 24-volt supply of the drive is switched on again.
